### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **59** of **211** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3fd803379817e495cd0011627c8b4a347f9dcc6a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4ebf7adadaf7c70641cfceb67ac03c136c61baf9` — the merge of head `ebeb778357c244efe0aa3e7d540cfc767875df3b` into base `3fd803379817e495cd0011627c8b4a347f9dcc6a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4ebf7adadaf7c70641cfceb67ac03c136c61baf9 && git checkout 4ebf7adadaf7c70641cfceb67ac03c136c61baf9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3fd803379817e495cd0011627c8b4a347f9dcc6a ebeb778357c244efe0aa3e7d540cfc767875df3b && git checkout -B drift-repro 3fd803379817e495cd0011627c8b4a347f9dcc6a && git merge --no-ff ebeb778357c244efe0aa3e7d540cfc767875df3b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3fd803379817e495cd0011627c8b4a347f9dcc6a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

`derivedTrend` at :684 to :688 is computed from `fetchedValue` and `previousValue`, which `invert` never touches), `pages.md` at this head (the three cut sentences and the paragraphs that already carry them) and `dashboards.md` (the heading "Period-over-period — `compareTo`" at :227). The head is mergeable and clean against today's `main` (merge-tree clean); none of the files `main` moved since the merge-base is in this diff.

### ① Derived judgments

- **S1: the sentence is true of the renderer** - right. The widget shows `1 - value` under `invert` but derives the trend from the raw aggregate and its previous-period value, so the arrow and the polarity colour both follow the raw number. The example is right as well: an error rate shown as uptime rises when things get worse, so its good direction is `lower`. The TSDoc and the describe say the same thing in one sentence each; the describe is the one that ships (`component.mdx` regenerated by `check:docs`, the json-schema built from it is not git-tracked and needs no regeneration here).
- **S2: the pointer and its payment** - right. The `object-metric` catalogue row now names `polarity` and links the `compareTo` section of `dashboards.md`, where the tile's `polarity` bullet lives. The three deletions each remove a sentence the same file still states: "id-scoped CSS at render time" (:238) carries "the CSS is scoped to it"; "Responsive lives in the breakpoint maps" (:251) carries the "responsive via the model" comment; the tier table's `react` row ("real React", JS runs) beside the `html` row ("constrained JSX, parsed, never executed") carries "it is real JS, not constrained JSX". Token count 5689 before and after against the 5692 ceiling in `check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`, which is not edited; the ratchet gate runs in `Lint & Repo Gates`. Warren's ruling A (cut duplicates first, raise only by the remainder) is followed with no remainder.
- **Accept-set: nothing an author writes moves** - right. The describe text changes, the enum, default and renderer do not. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right.
- **Check-runs as gate verdicts** - read as above; every run on this head completed and none is red, cancelled or in progress at the read.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/spec` patch, `@objectstack/skills` patch** - accepted. The spec entry is the lane's precedent for a describe-only change whose text ships in the built package (measured by the dev in dist and json-schema, both in `files[]`); the skills entry covers the shipped rule file.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Tier H by `skills/**`** - the seat posts its ACCEPT and requests os-zhuang / hotlong; a human approval lands it. This record is the review that ACCEPT names.
- **Serial overlap with #28334 on `content/docs/references/ui/component.mdx`** - both PRs regenerate that page (different rows). Whichever lands second merges `main` and re-runs `check:generated`; no hand-written hunk is shared, so no delta review is owed for that alone.
- **The link anchor is hand-computed and no gate holds it** - `dashboards.md#period-over-period--compareto` is the slug GitHub derives from the heading at :227 (em dash and backticks dropped, the two spaces becoming two hyphens), and it is the first cross-file link in the `objectstack-ui` rules. Correct today; if the heading is ever reworded the link goes stale silently. Not owed here.
- **Out of scope, as the card ruled** - whether the arrow should follow the displayed number when `invert` and `compareTo` are both set stays unmeasured; the describe now states the current behaviour, which is what an author needs to declare polarity correctly.
- **No name approval owed** - no new key.

**Verdict reasoning.** One true sentence about the renderer, placed where the key is declared and in the page generated from it; one pointer in the skill paid for by three exact duplicates in the same file with the token ceiling untouched; patch entries for both shipped surfaces; the head is clean against `main` and every check is green or skipped.
